edition.alertText: Trump rules out Sunday Iran strike but warns he may 'finish them off'; Brent eases to $115 after $117 weekly peak; IRGC claims 2 supertankers hit mines (4.5M bbl cargo); ~492 vessels waiting outside strait; Qatari mediators in Tehran as Iran sends mixed signals on reopening

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 240 with Iran sending contradictory diplomatic signals while shipping attacks continued at record pace. On October 24, Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed two supertankers struck naval mines south of the strait, carrying an estimated 4.5 million barrels of crude — both vessels reportedly suffered engine-room explosions and were left disabled. Iran warned that the tankers had used an 'unauthorized route' and said it would 'under no circumstances' allow US warships into the Persian Gulf. CENTCOM denied the mine claims and said Admiral Brad Cooper visited the strait on October 25 to inspect operations. The Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC) reported approximately 492 vessels waiting outside the strait as of October 25, with visible AIS traffic in the single digits to low double digits — far below the pre-crisis baseline of 85 transits per day. UKMTO recorded 18,049 anomalous AIS positions in its weekly overview published October 23, while Windward detected 293 vessels affected by GPS jamming on October 21 alone. Despite the chaos, Kpler data shows Middle East crude flows largely recovered to pre-war levels, though oil products remain about 50% below pre-war volumes. CENTCOM continued to claim a 95% transit success rate through its facilitated corridor, reporting 101 US-facilitated transits from October 22 to 24.

Oil markets pulled back on Monday after a fierce weekly rally. Brent crude settled at $116.72 on Friday — its highest close since April and up roughly 6% for the week — before easing to around $115.16 in early Monday Asian trade (down 1.34%), while WTI dipped to $101.67 (down 1.55%) after settling at $103.27 on Friday. The rally was fueled by Iran's 7-tanker attack claims on October 22, the 2-supertanker mine strikes on October 24, and Houthi escalation against Saudi targets. Gold eased to around $4,006 per ounce after safe-haven flows pushed it above $4,100 earlier in the week. VLCC tanker rates remained near record levels around $1.4 million per day for Gulf-to-East Asia routes, with freight adding $33–41 per barrel to delivered crude cost — more than a quarter of the delivered price. The EIA raised its Q4 Brent forecast to $105 (up $14 from September), while HSBC lifted its 2026 Brent outlook to $90 with a $120 stalemate scenario. US gasoline averaged $4.29 per gallon nationally with diesel at $6.35 — the highest since the 2022 spike. The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve sat at its lowest level since 1982, with the Energy Department authorizing an exchange of up to 400,000 barrels.

Geopolitical tensions seesawed between escalation threats and diplomatic overtures over the weekend. On Friday, US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack said a strike on Iran 'could happen this weekend,' prompting Trump to first raise the possibility of attacking 'as soon as Sunday' before ruling it out on October 25, saying 'there will be no strike today' while framing the choice as whether to 'make a deal or finish them off.' Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said Tehran 'has never left the negotiating table' but accused Washington of imposing 'unilateral demands.' Iran's ambassador to Pakistan said Tehran would reopen the strait within seven days if the US lifts its blockade, eases oil export restrictions, releases frozen assets, and ends hostilities — but Iran's Mehr News Agency denied any proposal had been sent, calling such reports 'a lie and fabrication.' Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran on Sunday to try to restart diplomacy. On the military front, Saudi Arabia intercepted a Houthi missile barrage near Mecca, and the death toll from the October 19 Houthi attack on a Yemeni government training camp in Shabwa rose to 73 killed with 14 still missing. Saudi Arabia postponed the Future Investment Initiative conference (originally scheduled October 26–29) to next year. European and Middle Eastern foreign ministers meeting in Istanbul on October 23 opposed renewed strikes on Iran, with Germany, France, and the UK saying they are ready to negotiate with Tehran.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased to ~$810/tonne by end-September from $1,000+ peak but remain far above pre-war levels. Mosaic idling South Fort Meade phosphate plant (Florida) for 6+ months from Dec 8 due to sulfur shortage. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Only 8 urea vessels left Gulf waters in September. ~850kt urea stranded across Iran and Arabian Gulf by mid-July (ICIS). 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). UNCTAD warns Hormuz disruption + El Niño could cut global harvests; fertilizer price volatility ahead of planting seasons threatens developing countries. Italian farmers blocking refineries over diesel.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: Qatar LNG exports still crippled — QatarEnergy signed historic deal to buy 4M tonnes/yr US LNG from Cheniere through 2054. Dutch TTF gas near €90/MWh. Japan's trade deficit doubled to ¥2.82T ($17.8B) on higher energy costs. Forbes warns next risk for US LNG is demand, not supply, as price dislocations persist.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint.
